query: Watch the Other Hand At the Gilded Newt, Corvin rolls a coin across his knuckles, and then it's in your pocket, and then it's back in his. "Grandfather's trick," he says. "I'd teach it to a saint, if the saint promised to only use it on people who deserve it." The jokes stop. "Do you promise?" Promise, and learn it You promise. He teaches you over three drinks you don't pay for, and by the last one you lift his coin without him feeling it. He looks at you for a long moment. "Don't make me sorry," he says, quietly. "Not that one, Corvin." "Saint," he says, fondly, and the coin goes back in his own pocket. He buys the next round anyway. You suspect he's relieved.
